Area.evidence_source: Wearing a mask was reportedly an important aspect of adhering to masculine norms of socialization. Most men were described as conscientious with a quiet or shy personality. They had a propensity to hide or suppress emotions; however, in order to socialize they would wear a mask or a cutout cardboard version as a coping strategy. Attitudes and beliefs of a rural masculinity, such as self-reliance, stoicism and a strong work ethic, and describing farmers as battlers and heroes are strongly embedded within the sociocultural norms of the occupation. For farm owners, there was a sense that farmers possessed a strong sense of self-worth in the role of a provider and attached importance to being a good farmer. X was a quiet man . . . a battler. . . always such a hard worker all his life . . . and didn't like to have other people do things for him . . . . Anger went inward instead of coming out . . . he was a very private person, and he couldn't cope with not being able to work . . . . If he wasn't on a tractor making hay or doing something with the cattle, he was out with a hoe in his hand. He loved his farm . . . . Farming and his family was number one in his life. Anything else just hopped in line behind that . . . . (F3)
